text.en:
Latha poured tea through a strainer and the tea leaves stayed behind. Later at the sea she saw workers letting sea water dry in shallow pans.
White salt was left behind.
"One way keeps the solid back and the other lets the water go," she said.

Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid using a filter such as a cloth, paper or strainer. The liquid passes through and the solid stays behind. Muddy water can be filtered to make it clearer.
Evaporation separates a dissolved solid from a liquid. When salt water is heated or left in the sun, the water evaporates as vapour and the salt is left behind. This is how salt is made from sea water.
Often we use both: filter the sand away, then evaporate the water to get the dissolved salt.
Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid using a filter. The liquid goes through.
Evaporation separates a dissolved solid. The water goes into air and the solid is left.
Salt is made from sea water by evaporation in the Sun.
We can use both methods one after the other.

problem.en: How will you get salt from a mixture of sand and salt dissolved in water?

text.en: First pour the mixture through a filter. The sand stays on the paper.
The clear liquid is salt water.
Heat or leave it in the sun. The water evaporates and the salt is left.

prompt.en: A friend says salt can be filtered out of salt water. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Salt is dissolved, so it passes through the filter with the water.
We must evaporate the water to get salt.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a filter stops dissolved things.

points.en: Filtration removes insoluble solids from liquids.
